cards.headline: A gospel refrain from 1964, rebuilt in a Mott Street home studio
cards.snippet: 'One of These Mornings' began as track six on 18 (2002), the album Moby recorded at his home studio on Mott Street in Manhattan after the 21-month Play tour. Where Play was built on samples of old records, he worked with live singers here, and the voice on this track is Dianne McCaulley's. The whole song is built on a single gospel refrain — one of these mornings, it won't be very long, you will look for me and I'll be gone — the couplet Cassietta George wrote and sang with the Caravans on 'Walk Around Heaven All Day' in 1964.
cards.context: 18 is a guest-vocalist album — Sinéad O'Connor, Angie Stone and Azure Ray are its marquee singers; McCaulley's is its least-known voice.

cards.headline: Re-recorded with Patti LaBelle, then adopted by television
cards.snippet: Four years after 18, Moby re-recorded the song with Patti LaBelle for a film soundtrack, stretching it from 3:12 to four minutes; issued on the soundtrack album in July 2006, that is the version most listeners know. Television then kept it in circulation for two decades: it bookends the Torchwood episode 'To the Last Man,' closes a Person of Interest episode, and recurred in Without a Trace. The official audio's comment thread has since become something else — a memorial wall where listeners post their own losses.
cards.context: Consequence ranked the song sixth among Moby's ten greatest tracks, calling him 'a bluesman at heart.'

cards.headline: The thread's most-liked thought: sad music, taken to feel better
cards.snippet: Life is so ironic that we listen to sad music to feel better
cards.context: Its top reply refines the thought — the point is not to feel better, but to know we are not alone in our heartache.

replies.author: @sloponyblues
replies.text: We listen to sad songs not to feel better, but as a communal shared suffering of loss, to know that we are not alone in our heartache

replies.author: @bucky414
replies.text: Nope it is to remember we were once alive, till life took it from us. We survive not knowing. Stay safe

cards.headline: Posted the night her dog of fifteen years died
cards.snippet: My dog, Tom, passed two hours ago. Fifteen years of love, happiness and joy. This is the song I needed to fall asleep to. Love each other while you're still here, one of these mornings... you won't be.
cards.context: Her sign-off turns the refrain's promise back on the reader: one of these mornings, you won't be here either.

replies.author: @ursula1893
replies.text: Ohhh....I KNOW this place very well. Our so called pets are family members in every sense of the word. I'm so sorry 😞. I lost my Mini Schnauzer over 15 years ago. I still miss 😢 Max today....every day....forever!

cards.headline: 'Makes me happy in 2014' — its replies keep renewing the claim
cards.snippet: Moby's sampling style of early 2000s is the thing that makes me happy in 2014.
cards.context: Its replies run a relay across the years — still happy in 2018, in 2020's chaos, in 2021, in 2022.

cards.headline: 'If you ever feel the need to have a good cry' — answered by a smile
cards.snippet: If you ever feel the need to have a good cry.....
cards.context: Its top reply disagrees outright — for them the song is triumphant, and its tears are tears of relief.

replies.author: @user-pi5hs4uv8e
replies.text: I have to actually smile. No offense to you. It's a triumphant song for me. Maybe tears of relief

cards.headline: The Patti LaBelle version: a minute longer, and the one the world kept
cards.snippet: Moby re-recorded his own song in 2006 with Patti LaBelle — 4:01 against the original's 3:12, her vocal produced by Mark Batson — for the Miami Vice soundtrack album; it appears on no Moby studio album. One listener: "Sweet sweet sound of Patti LaBelle with this piece!!! Beautiful find!"
cards.context: Its own upload thread is a second memorial wall — the same refrain, a separate congregation from the original's.

version.versionLabel: Moby feat. Patti LaBelle - One of these Mornings

cards.headline: Miami Vice (2006): the speedboat run to Havana
cards.snippet: The LaBelle version plays over the film's signature sequence — Crockett and Isabella's speedboat run to Havana — and returns under the closing credits; in Mann's director's cut it also opens the film, replacing the Nonpoint 'In the Air Tonight' cover.
cards.context: A fan upload of the boat scene alone has been watched 1.8 million times.
